data: Tiny — just 504 km across — but the most reflective body in the solar system and one of the strongest candidates for present-day habitability beyond Earth. Cassini flew directly through plumes erupting from four 130-km-long fractures at the south pole; the spectrometer detected molecular hydrogen, organics including methane, salts, and silica nanograins indicating active hydrothermal chemistry on the ocean floor. The ocean is in direct contact with rocky seafloor — the same energy and chemistry conditions that gave rise to life at Earth's own deep-sea hydrothermal vents.
Pristine water-ice crust over a global subsurface ocean; south-polar 'tiger stripe' fractures venting plumes of water vapour, organics, salts, silica nanograins, and molecular hydrogen.
Enceladus is in 2:1 mean-motion resonance with Dione — the forced eccentricity (0.0047) drives the tidal flexing that powers the south-polar cryovolcanic plumes.
How stretched the orbit is — zero is a perfect circle, one is a parabolic escape.
